name: Rigisamus
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rigisamus was a god of the British and continental Celts. Followers also called him Rigonemetis. Both names were used for the same divinity. His name signified most kingly or most regal. Dedications to him are found in Britain and in France. The Romans equated him with the warrior god Mars. A second divine name, Rigonemetis, meant king of the sacred grove. The records of this obscure god are thin but real.
